steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles, exactly 5 years after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand. It was primarily negotiated by three leaders: Wilson (USA), Clemenceau (France), and Lloyd George (Britain). Their conflicting aims made a balanced settlement almost impossible. | Key Fact: The Treaty of Versailles had five main categories: War Guilt, Reparations, Military restrictions, Territorial losses, and the League of Nations. Germans called it the "Diktat" (dictated peace) because they were not allowed to negotiate the terms. | Key Fact: Germany lost 13% of its European territory, 10% of its population, and all of its overseas empire.
